name: default-swapy
title: Draggable Stats Bento
description: Nine flat-colour cards of different widths form a tight bento grid mixing big metrics, client praise and a balance panel. Dragging any tile onto another swaps their places and the grid closes up around them.
use: A landing or overview page wants a lively mosaic of metrics that visitors can shuffle.
avoid: Every card's copy, colour and width is fixed in the file, and the new order is never saved.
a11y: Tiles are dragged by their body with no keyboard route, and the colourful cards expose no roles or names. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A packed twelve-column grid of rounded flat tiles in emerald, grey, pale blue, pink, yellow, purple and royal blue, with white, black or yellow type. Widths vary from a narrow 57K tile to a wide card holding two portrait blocks.
behaves: Dragging a card by its body lifts it and marks the slot beneath; releasing over another slot swaps the two and every tile snaps back to the same fixed height. The new order is only announced in the console and lasts until reload.
customise: No props: the nine cards, their palette and column spans are written into the file as an items array of ready-made nodes.
weight: light: Nine static colour tiles and a drag handler that only runs during a move.
demo: Project Views 4.875, New Users 57K, 54 daily clients, Trusted By 500+ Users and the font SK-Modernist.
issues: Swaps are only logged to the console, so the arrangement is lost on reload.
Every slot is a fixed 256 px tall, so longer card copy would overflow.
The bottom row of tiles is clipped by the frame edge in every frame.
polishWhy: Lively palette and a tidy mosaic; clashing saturated colours and cramped headers feel unrefined.

frames.note: The bottom row of tiles is clipped at the frame edge, so their lower borders never show.
